preamble: The shift from the voiceless uvular fricative [χ] to the voiceless glottal fricative [h] is a process of debuccalization (lenition): the oral constriction at the uvula is lost and only glottal friction remains. Fula turned Proto-Fula-Sereer *x into h (*xande 'today' > hannde), which Sereer keeps as x, and Northern Tai languages such as Standard Zhuang have h for Proto-Tai *χ (*χiːŋᴬ 'ginger' > hing).

examples.note: Sereer xas. Pozdniakov counts 32 roots with Sereer x ~ Fula h: the postvelar fricative merged with the velar series' h in Fula.
Southwestern Tai has kʰ (Thai ขิง, ขึ้น, เขี้ยว); *q instead gives Zhuang k (gaeu 'horn').

sources: Ladefoged, P., & Maddieson, I. (1996). The Sounds of the World's Languages. Blackwell. https://www.wiley.com/en-us/The+Sounds+of+the+World%27s+Languages-p-9780631198154
Pozdniakov, K. (2022). Proto-Fula-Sereer: Lexicon, morphophonology, and noun classes. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5820515
